Evaluate the triple integral 
${∭}_{R}{y}^{2}\,dV$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the front one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216491/assets/2427e053c0e2d808b32db5d7fedf81365e7e50f0b3f2dc61598ad1795394686e.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 2+2y-z\},
$$

where

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1\}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216491/assets/145f0d494ffe24de84e3a289b3a7316d3f4933f193d734aed118609f7fb9f94f.png)

Hence, we can express the region $R$ as

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le 2+2y-z\}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2+2y-z}{y}^{2}\,dx\,dz\,dy.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x$, treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2+2y-z}{y}^{2}\,dx\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2+2y-z}{y}^{2}\,dx]dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}[x]_{x=0}^{x=2+2y-z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}(2+2y-z)\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}2{y}^{2}+2{y}^{3}-{y}^{2}z\,dz\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}2{y}^{2}+2{y}^{3}-{y}^{2}z\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}2{y}^{2}+2{y}^{3}-{y}^{2}z\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[2{y}^{2}z+2{y}^{3}z-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2{y}^{2}+2{y}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2}+2{y}^{3}\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2}+2{y}^{3}\,dy & ={[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{3}+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2})-0 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
